Aerial Wildlife 
Survey Report 
Wildlife Management Unit 520 Moose Aerial Survey (2018) 
 
 
Background 
Cadotte Lakes-Otter Lakes Wildlife Management Unit 520 (WMU 520) in the Peace Region covers an area of 
10,942.5 km2, with 2,000 km2 comprising caribou range and 842 km2 designated as a Key Wildlife and Biodiversity 
Zone. The WMU also has a Road Corridor Wildlife Sanctuary on the Peace River Pulp Road C. The northern 
boreal mixedwood forest is the predominant ecoregion in the  WMU, with a smaller portion of the boreal hig hlands 
region represented. First Nations  reserves present in WMU 520 include Woodland Cree (No.226 -228), Swampy 
Lake (No. 236), Loon Lake (No. 235) and Loon Prairie (No. 237). 
A survey for moose was last conducted for WMU 520 in 2011 using the random stra tified block methodology 
(Random Block). The moose population was estimated to have 2,326 individuals, a density of 0.21 moose/km 2, 
and a bull:cow:calf ratio of 34:100:44 (Moyles and Stavne 2012). See Table 1 for previous moos e survey estimates 
for WMU 520. 
The objective of the 2018 survey was to assess the status of the moose population in WMU 520 by determining 
estimates for abundance, density and the age-sex composition. 
 
Survey Method 
An aerial survey for moose was conducted from January 15 th to 18th, 2018 using distance sampling techniques 
(Buckland et al., 2001, 2010). A total of 267 north-south transect lines (survey effort = 2,056 km) were flown. 
Moose were classified by age class (adult or calf) and sex. Other wildlife sightings were recorded.  
 
Results 
A total of 187 moose were observed in 114 groups. The encounter rate was 0.054 moose/km 2 (90% confidence 
interval (CI) of 0.04 – 0.07). The estimated density was 0.16 moose/km 2 (90% CI 0.116 – 0.218) and the estimated 
abundance was 1,738 individuals (90% CI 1,267 – 2,385). The coefficient of variation for both density and 
abundance was 0.16 (Table 2). A total of 182 moose were successfully classified and the bull:cow:calf ratio was 
estimated to be 78:100:52.
